subject: Request for penetration test report access / NDA and redaction discussion
messages:
From: Tom Harris <tharris@acme-corp.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request for penetration test report and NDA

Hi Karthik,

Acme's security team is completing our vendor risk review for the Q3 integration. We need to review Redwood's most recent penetration test report and executive summary to complete a control assessment (SOC/ISO mapping). Can you share the full report or an executive summary? Our security team requires either:

- Full report behind a mutual NDA, or
- Redacted executive summary without sensitive findings.

Please let me know Redwood's process for sharing this material, any required redaction policy, and typical turnaround time. If you have a standard mutual NDA, please send.

Thanks,
Tom Harris
Senior Security Analyst
Acme Corp
security@acme-corp.com

[Attachment: Acme_Vendor_Questionnaire.pdf (pdf)]
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Tom Harris <tharris@acme-corp.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request for penetration test report and NDA

Tom — thanks for the note. Happy to help. Quick summary of our standard approach: 

- We can share a redacted executive summary (high-level scope, methodology, overall risk posture, remediation status) without an NDA within 2 business days.
- The full penetration test report (detailed findings, PoC, IPs) requires a signed mutual NDA and a short legal review; typical turnaround after received signature is 1–3 business days.

Looping in Dev (security) and Evelyn (legal) to confirm redaction levels and remediation details.

Proposed next steps: 
1) If Acme is OK with the NDA, please send your standard mutual NDA link or sign ours (I can share via DocuSign).
2) If you'd prefer the exec summary first, we'll send a redacted PDF within 48 business hours.

Which do you prefer?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

From: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Request for penetration test report and NDA

Karthik — legal here. For clarity on our redaction policy and sharing controls: 

- Executive summary: we allow sharing of a redacted executive summary that removes any exploit code, full request/response payloads, exact configuration values, and specific IP/hostname identifiers. The summary will still include scope (engines tested, major components), overall severity distribution, and remediation status.
- Full report: requires a mutual NDA with standard confidentiality and purpose-of-use clauses. We do not permit recipient distribution beyond the named security contacts.

Please do not share any scanned attachments that contain raw logs or screenshots with sensitive tokens. If Acme insists on fuller access, we require: signed NDA, list of named recipients, and an e-mail acceptance of our limited-scope usage covenant. Once we have that, we will schedule a secure file transfer (DocuSign + S3 pre-signed link or secure box).

Dev — confirm whether any high-severity items are still pending so we can be explicit in the exec summary.

— Evelyn Hart
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
evelyn_hart@redwood.com

From: dev_patel@redwood.com
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Request for penetration test report and NDA

Evelyn / Karthik — quick security status: 

- The latest internal pentest engagement (conducted externally by ZeroWall, report dated 2025-05-21) identified one critical finding in the deprecated telemetry ingestion path. That finding has a remediation PR open and is scheduled for release in the 2025-06-18 maintenance window.
- Three high findings were closed as of 2025-06-01 and verified by the vendor.
- No unresolved severity-1 findings beyond the telemetry item.

For the exec summary we can state: "one critical issue in telemetry ingestion (remediation scheduled), three high issues remediated and verified," without exposing repro steps or IPs. If Acme needs the full technical appendix, they must sign the NDA and agree to the named-recipient constraint.

— Dev Patel
Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com

Tom — thanks for the quick turnaround. Acme's approach works for us. Two options (pick one):

A) Sign mutual NDA and we'll provide the full report via secure transfer (DocuSign link I will send; we will require the named recipients list). Expect file delivery within 1 business day after signature plus legal review (typically same day).

B) Receive the redacted executive summary now (attached) while you review the NDA. The attached PDF is intentionally redacted per our policy (no PoC, no IPs, no logs) and includes the remediation status from Dev.

I've attached the redacted executive summary for immediate review: Redwood_Pentest_Exec_Summary_v1_redacted.pdf (attached). If you prefer option A, reply with the names/emails of intended recipients and I will initiate DocuSign for the mutual NDA (we can also accept your standard mutual NDA if you prefer; I've included a DocuSign template link below to speed things up).
